Exercise A

Reading: The Project Manager's Email

Read the email from the project manager, then answer the questions.

Subject: Summary – options to recover the delay on Riverside Offices

Hi all,

Thanks for joining yesterday's site meeting. Here is a summary of where we are.

Heavy rain in October has put the Riverside Offices project three weeks behind schedule. The client expects the building to be handed over on 28 February, and the contract includes a penalty of £5,000 for every week we finish late.

We have a shortlist of three options: adding weekend shifts for the current team, bringing in a second steelwork subcontractor, or asking the client to move the handover date.

To keep the decision objective, we agreed to use a weighted decision matrix. Each option is scored from 1 to 5 against four criteria: time saved, cost, site safety and build quality. Because a late handover would trigger the penalty, time saved carries the highest weighting (40%). Safety carries 30%.

We also identified the key stakeholders. The client, the subcontractors and our health and safety manager must all be consulted, and the health and safety manager has to approve any plan that increases working hours on site.

At this stage, the second subcontractor has the highest overall score (4.2), mainly because it saves the most time. However, it is also the most expensive option, so there is a clear trade-off between speed and cost. Weekend shifts scored 3.6 and cost about 40% less, but tired workers increase the risk of accidents.

My recommendation is that we should get quotes from two steelwork subcontractors this week before we commit. We ought to have the quotes by Friday, which still leaves time to start work on site in early December.

Please send me any comments by Thursday.

Best regards,
Daniel Brooks
Project Manager
